newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: General Gold suspends mining over costs.
newsitem.headline: General Gold suspends mining over costs.

text.p: General Gold Resources NL, citing high operating costs, said on Thursday it would suspend gold mining operations at its Mount Monger project in Western Australia in favour of exploration work.

General Gold and partner Ramsgate Resources NL are also considering selling a mill at Mount Monger and building a new plant at a cost of about A$10 million closer to the Randalls tenements where the new exploration programme is focused.

Mount Monger has been producing about 50,000 ounces of gold a year, all from the Maxwells open pit mine located in its Randalls tenements block. But a combination of a low gold price, the prospects of a new gold royalty in Western Australia and other taxes and transportation costs had made mining of the pit uneconomical, General Gold Managing Director Cliff Harding said.
"We see the main focus for our activity is really proving up sufficient resources at Randalls to build a new plant out there," Harding told Reuters.
He said the partners would spend A$5 million on exploration over the next 12 months to boost resources at Randalls.

Gold producion has been coming solely from the Maxwells pit, located in the Randalls tenements, creating high operating costs because the ore had to be shipped 40 km to the mill at Mount Monger, Harding said.
Mining at the Maxwells pit will be suspended in about 30 days in order to conserve the resource for "future, more profitable operations," Harding said.
He said the partners were taking a long-term view of the future potential of the Mount Monger project.
"Having a plant at Randalls will enable us to reduce the cut-off grade below our current trucking grade, substantially increasing the resource in that way," he said.
The resource at the Randalls deposit currently stands at 3.025 million tonnes, grading 3.2 grammes of gold per tonne, containing about 315,900 ounces of gold, he said.
Harding said operating costs were nearing about A$400 an ounce, taking into account transportation, leaving little room for profits. Gold currently fetches about A$450 an ounce.

"It's by far a better strategy to conserve that ore, drop the cut-off grade make it bigger and a slightly lower grade," he said. "With things like gold royalties upon us and diesel fuel rebates under attack by government and a lousy gold price, you must look to the future to have a more profitable operation."

In the meantime, General Gold and Ramsgate have proposed development in July of the nearby Christmas Flat open pit mine, adjacent to the Mount Monger mill. "At the end of March we had about 10,000 ounces in reserve at Christmas Flat and that would give us three or four months of processing work," Harding said.
Ramsgate is 55.6 percent owned by fellow Perth-based miner Westgold Resources NL.
